items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept secret?
premises: The teaching is to be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The mortal world contains the lowest of men
items.inference: This teaching must be carefully hidden in the mortal world among unworthy people.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: What qualifications must a recipient meet before receiving this teaching?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient should be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: Only a previously accomplished person tested for one year is fit to receive the teaching.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa
The section is numbered fifth
The section is a chapter
items.inference: This marks the end of the fifth chapter of the text from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: Through whose grace has the determination of Kaula been understood?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Understanding arose by that lord's grace
The object understood is the determination of Kaula
items.inference: The speaker has understood the determination of Kaula through the grace of the lord of Kaulas.
items.plain_english: O lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have understood the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the soul?
premises: The soul has been declared in the teaching
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both who the soul is and what its true nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is questioned
A complete explanation is requested
items.inference: The speaker asks to be told fully where the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the true nature of that being?
premises: That being is supreme
That being is partless and eternal
That being is free from disease and stainless
items.inference: The being in question is defined by supreme, partless, eternal, and pure qualities.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in terms of haṃsa and śakti?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That supreme soul is identified as haṃsa
That soul is also called the individual of power
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as the haṃsa, the individual embodiment of power.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul which is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual of power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated?
premises: The vital air is filled with breath
It is situated in a locus
That locus is all living beings
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What identity is ascribed to the soul upon merely leaving the body?
premises: The condition is merely leaving the body
At that moment a designation is given
The designation is supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, that being is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and perceived according to tradition?
premises: Something is heard in the ear
The addressee is the goddess
It has come down through traditional succession
items.inference: The teaching is heard in the ear as it has been transmitted through tradition.
items.plain_english: O goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the traditional lineage.

items.question: What effect does merely hearing this knowledge have for the practitioner?
premises: The means is this knowledge alone
The knowledge is heard
The goddess is addressed directly
items.inference: Even merely hearing this knowledge is presented as efficacious.
uncertainties: The main clause continues in the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, when it is heard...

rows.grounds: time duration; compound ṣaṣ+māsa with ablative sense
object or state associated with renunciation

items.question: What practice and renunciant state are required over six months?
premises: Practice should continue for six months
The practitioner is specified by a relative clause
The state is free from bondage and associated with the ochre robe
items.inference: One who practices for six months in a state free from bondage attains the stated result.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of kāṣāyaṃ is somewhat compressed in this verse.
items.plain_english: But whoever practices for six months, in the ochre robe and free from bondage...

items.question: What benefits result from sustained practice of this teaching?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
The practitioner gains association with yogis
This follows the prescribed practice
items.inference: Sustained practice leads to freedom from disease and union with yogis.
items.plain_english: He becomes freed from all diseases and attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: The speaker addresses Bhairavī
The subject is the practice concerning the soul
This practice has been told to her
items.inference: The teaching on the practice of the soul has now been communicated to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of resolved person may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient is endowed with all states
The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: The teaching should be given to a person endowed with all states and firm resolve.
uncertainties: The case shift between genitive and locative is notable in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a resolved mind.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs be withheld?
premises: The Kaula essence is identified
It originates from the yoginīs
It is explicitly not to be given
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given indiscriminately.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation of sambhavam to sāraṃ is compressed.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after receiving this knowledge?
premises: The speaker refers to her own body
The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
The body is now declared pure
items.inference: Receiving the knowledge has purified the speaker's body from the veil of ignorance.
uncertainties: The form deham appears where a nominative would be expected.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious knowledge about overcoming time is now sought?
premises: The speaker expresses a wish to hear
The topic concerns time
The desired teaching is the auspicious deception of time
items.inference: The speaker now seeks the auspicious teaching on overcoming or deceiving time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious teaching on the overcoming of time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the destruction of death through this teaching?
premises: The speaker promises to tell
There is no doubt
Death is destroyed by this means
items.inference: The teaching is asserted to destroy death without doubt.
items.plain_english: I will tell you without doubt how death is destroyed.

items.question: How can even a wise person be affected at the point of nectar?
premises: The locus is the tip of nectar
The means involves the essence of juice
Even a wise person may be burning
items.inference: Even a wise person can be afflicted at the point of nectar by this essence.
uncertainties: The imagery of amṛta+agraṃ and rasa+agreṇa is esoteric and compressed.
items.plain_english: Even a wise person may be burned at the tip of nectar by the essence of that juice.

items.question: What bodily technique is prescribed for drawing in the vital air?
premises: The locus is the root of tongue and palate
An action is performed there
The vital air should be drunk slowly
items.inference: The practitioner should slowly draw in the vital air at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the vital air.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this technique for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The condition is sustained practice
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: Practicing this technique for one year destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to poison is attained through this perfected practice?
premises: The body may be bitten by great serpents
Poison would normally enter the body
In this case poison does not enter
items.inference: The perfected practitioner gains immunity so that poison does not enter the body even when bitten by great serpents.
items.plain_english: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
